issue.title: agent: stash originals lost on restore failure and malformed stash replaced

comments.body:
Re-verified at current main (`eb1b83000`) — rebased with zero drift (range-diff identical; nothing upstream touched `internal/agent` in between), patch bytes unchanged.

| Element | Evidence at `eb1b83000` |
| --- | --- |
| Rebase | `hunt-20261114-d1-4258` = `eb1b83000` + the patch, range-diff identical |
| git am | replays on a clean `upstream/main` to a byte-identical tree |
| Tests | `internal/agent` in full: the only red is the pre-existing `TestMothX` (documented standing red, same on the base commit); the new test green, `-race` on it ok; `go vet`, `gofmt` clean; `GOOS` linux/darwin/windows `nogui` builds ok |
| Ablation | the three product files (`claude.go`, `codex.go`, `stash.go`) reverted with the tests kept: `TestDisconnectFailureKeepsStashedOriginals` fails on both its `claude` and `codex` subtests — restored, green |
| Siblings | the `peek`/`forgetValues` consumers re-scanned at this tip: the 5 call sites stand, no new `unroute`-family callers upstream |
| Real path | unchanged from the patch post: mode 1 (delete + restore-write before the restored write) is reproduced by the test's subtests; a real cross-process concurrent stash write (mode 3) stays not verified, listed as left |

Branch with the commit: [hunt-20261114-d1-4258](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt-20261114-d1-4258) (head `57ef507fd47213d8`). Patch bytes are identical to the post above — SHA-256 first 16: `c9663118cd5ad6ac`.

Attribution: AI-written; I've read the whole diff and can answer questions on it myself. Please keep the author (`ggbdpq`) or add `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

Face 1 landed in v0.1.4130: @ggbdpq's 1dbd3bb07 (authorship kept), plus my f62e93b8a. Claude Code's and Codex's Disconnect now `peek` the stashed originals and take them out of the stash only after the write that puts them back succeeds. A failed write leaves them stashed for the next try.

Review fix (f62e93b8a): with the patch alone, Claude Code's Unwire left the stashed model behind when it neither put the model back nor removed magpie's. That happens when the stash kept one of magpie's models and the user has since picked their own. Before the patch, `unroute` always took it out. `TestClaudeDisconnectLeavesNoModelStashed` is ok on main, red with the patch alone, and ok with the fix. `TestDisconnectFailureKeepsStashedOriginals` is red with main's claude.go, codex.go and stash.go, and ok at the head.

Still open here:
- Face 2: a malformed stash.json is still copied aside (`lastgood.KeepUnparsed`) before it is written over, as on main. That changed nothing new.
- Face 3: there is no cross-process stash lock yet.
- The other agents' restore paths have the same unstash-before-write shape, filed as #6601.

Keeping this open, for @skygunner too.

issue.title: agent: Disconnect's restore paths of other agents take originals out of the stash before writing them back (#4258 sibling)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Left by #4258's fix (ggbdpq's patch, landing with this batch): Claude Code's and Codex's Disconnect now keep the stashed originals until the write that puts them back has gone through. The other agents with a restore path still take their originals out of the stash before writing them back, so a write that fails there loses them the same way #4258 described:

- agy / Antigravity, ante, AstrBot, Cline, Claude Desktop restore paths in `internal/agent` (`unstash` before the restore write).

The fix is the same shape: `peek` the keys, write, then `forgetValues` only after the write succeeds; a test per agent that makes the restore write fail (read-only settings file) and checks the stash still has the original.
